edges.description: GBA1 mutations reduce or abolish glucocerebrosidase enzyme activity.
Loss of glucocerebrosidase activity impairs lysosomal degradation of glucosylceramide.
Very low residual GCase activity in severe genotypes permits neuronal glycosphingolipid storage.
intermediate_mechanisms: low residual GCase activity in neuronopathic genotypes

edges.description: Reduced GCase activity impairs lysosomal protein degradation and increases alpha-synuclein in experimental neuronal systems; this supports a possible Parkinson-risk mechanism rather than universal neuronopathic Gaucher pathology.
GCase-deficient stromal cells show lipid accumulation and altered mediator secretion in vitro.
Undegraded glucosylceramide accumulates primarily in macrophages.
GCase deficiency favors alternative conversion of glucosylceramide to glucosylsphingosine.
Lipid-laden macrophages become Gaucher cells.
Stored lipid and lipid-reactive antibodies can activate complement in experimental Gaucher disease.
Exposed glucosylceramide can act as an endogenous Mincle ligand in experimental myeloid systems.
intermediate_mechanisms: release or exposure of cellular glucosylceramide

edges.description: Gaucher cells infiltrate spleen and liver, causing reticuloendothelial organ enlargement.
Gaucher cell infiltration of marrow disrupts hematopoietic space and contributes to cytopenias.
Gaucher and activated monocyte/macrophage populations release cytokines, chemokines, chitotriosidase, and CCL18.
Marrow Gaucher-cell accumulation may contribute to focal ischemic injury through vascular compression. This is a proposed route; inflammatory and mechanical factors may also contribute.
Liver infiltration by Gaucher cells enlarges the liver.
Spleen infiltration by Gaucher cells enlarges the spleen.
Systemic disease burden may limit growth and weight gain in Type 1 disease.
Enlarged, infiltrated spleen contributes to sequestration of blood cells.
Marrow infiltration and splenic involvement reduce circulating platelet counts.
Marrow infiltration contributes to reduced red-cell output and anemia.
Cytopenias and systemic Gaucher disease burden can manifest as fatigue.
Inflammatory mediators stimulate bone resorption and contribute to skeletal disease.
Glucosylsphingosine is a candidate contributor to neuronal toxicity; the intervening injury processes and its relative importance versus other lipids remain incompletely established.
Sphingolipid imbalance, including sphingosine generated from glucosylsphingosine metabolism, contributes to skeletal toxicity.
Accumulated lysolipid can provide chronic antigenic stimulation.
Skeletal infiltration, bone crises, and infarction cause recurrent bone pain.
Dysregulated Gaucher skeletal remodeling lowers bone mass and produces osteopenia.
Low bone mass and disordered remodeling increase pathological fracture risk.
Abnormal skeletal remodeling produces the characteristic distal femur deformity.
Neuronal lipid storage and injury are accompanied by microgliosis and astrogliosis.
Neuronal lipid toxicity causes neuronal dysfunction and death, producing oculomotor, bulbar, pyramidal, seizure, and developmental phenotypes.
Activated microglia phagocytose impaired neurons in the Gba1 D409V/progranulin-null mouse model; the contribution to ordinary human neuronopathic disease remains qualified by the sensitized model.
Dysfunction of neuronal circuits controlling saccades contributes to oculomotor apraxia in chronic neuronopathic disease; the clinical cohort does not identify the intervening circuit lesion.
Chronic neuronopathic disease commonly affects horizontal supranuclear gaze.
Progressive neuronal dysfunction produces seizures and myoclonic epilepsy.
Chronic neuronopathic disease may progress to myoclonus epilepsy.
Bulbar dysfunction in acute neuronopathic disease causes swallowing impairment.
Pyramidal tract involvement produces progressive spasticity and rigidity.
Early neuronopathic injury alters psychomotor development.
Oculomotor pathway involvement may present as bilateral fixed strabismus.
Impaired alpha-synuclein proteostasis increases Parkinson disease risk and can manifest clinically as parkinsonism.
Hypersplenism contributes to anemia.
Splenic sequestration contributes to low platelet counts.
C5aR1 signaling increases glucosylceramide synthase production.
Complement signaling enhances inflammatory-cell recruitment and cytokine production.
Increased substrate synthesis adds to accumulation when degradation is deficient.
Chronic antigenic stimulation can contribute to clonal gammopathy.
Epiphyseal ischemic bone injury manifests as avascular osteonecrosis.
Bone infarction can produce severe bone crises.
Mincle-dependent myeloid signaling induces inflammatory cytokine production in vitro.
Stromal inflammatory mediators may influence local bone-cell homeostasis.
MGUS can progress to multiple myeloma; the reported ten-year progression estimate was similar to that of the general population.

nodes.description: Investigational pharmacologic enhancement of residual mutant GCase stability and activity. However, they usually cause abnormalities referred to as bone infarcts on long bones (metaphyses or diaphyses) and flat bones, and lesions referred to as avascular necrosis (AVN) on the epiphyses.
